title: God Method & Arrow Anti-Pattern (Deep Nesting)
fowlerPattern: Extract Method / Replace Conditional with Pipeline (Chain of Responsibility)
description: Single monolithic function `processOrderBatch()` spanning over 120 lines with 7 levels of nested if/else statements. It simultaneously handles order validation, stock checking, tax computation, discount resolution, payment gateway communication, and dispatching notifications.
justification: Violates the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP). Extreme cognitive load makes unit testing impossible without setting up 15 distinct interdependent mocks, creating high regression risk on every modification.
suggestedFix: Decompose the monolith into discrete, composable pipeline steps (Validation, InventoryReservation, Pricing, Payment, Fulfillment) orchestrated via a clean Pipeline pattern.
refactoredReference: Lines 120-210 in RefactoredOrderPipeline.ts (IOrderStep interface and OrderProcessingPipeline)

title: Primitive Obsession & Floating-Point Rounding Corruption
fowlerPattern: Replace Primitive with Object (Value Object: Money)
description: Monetary sums, discounts, and tax rates are represented as raw JavaScript IEEE 754 floating-point numbers (`let total = 0.0; total += price * (1 - discount)`), resulting in precision inaccuracies such as 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004.
justification: Financial and e-commerce systems cannot tolerate floating-point rounding errors which accumulate across line items and cause reconciliation failures with banking ledgers and payment gateways.
suggestedFix: Implement an immutable `Money` Value Object that encapsulates calculations in integer cents (or micro-units) and enforces standard rounding algorithms (e.g. Banker’s Rounding / Half-Even).

title: Quadratic $O(N \times M)$ Unindexed Inventory Search
description: For every order line item, the system scans the entire global inventory array linearly using `inventory.find(inv => inv.sku === item.sku)`. In a batch of 1,000 orders each having 5 items against a catalog of 20,000 products, this performs 100,000,000 array iterations.
justification: Creates severe CPU spikes and degrades API response time from tens of milliseconds to multiple seconds under heavy traffic.
suggestedFix: Pre-index the inventory catalog into an in-memory `Map<string, InventoryItem>` enabling $O(1)$ constant-time lookup, transforming the algorithm to $O(N + M)$ linear complexity.

title: Hardcoded Switch-Case Violation of Open-Closed Principle
description: Promotional discount rules (`SUMMER20`, `VIP_PLATINUM`, `FLASH_SALE`, `BULK_TIER`) are hardcoded in an imperative `switch(discountCode)` block with scattered magic numbers and nested date checks.
justification: Violates Open-Closed Principle (OCP). Adding or modifying any promotional rule requires modifying and redeploying the core order fulfillment class, risking breaking unrelated discount logic.
suggestedFix: Introduce an `IDiscountStrategy` interface and register dynamic discount strategies with priority weighting and eligibility evaluators.

title: Non-Transactional State Mutation & Phantom Stock Deduction
fowlerPattern: Unit of Work / Two-Phase Compensation Pattern
description: Global inventory quantities are decremented immediately before charging payment (`inv.stock -= item.qty`). If the payment gateway subsequently rejects the credit card or times out, the stock deduction is never rolled back, causing phantom inventory loss.
justification: Causes data corruption and phantom out-of-stock conditions in production where paying customers are prevented from purchasing available products.
suggestedFix: Implement a two-phase reservation lock mechanism: acquire an ephemeral reservation token; only commit stock upon confirmed payment capture, with automatic rollback compensation on failure.

title: PCI-DSS Compliance Breach: Plaintext Credit Card Logging
fowlerPattern: Introduce Redaction / Sensitive Data Masking Guard
description: The legacy audit logging function prints the full customer request including `order.paymentInfo.cardNumber` and `order.paymentInfo.cvv` to standard output and diagnostic logs via `console.log("Charging:", JSON.stringify(order))`.
justification: Critical security vulnerability violating PCI-DSS Requirement 3.4. Exposes plaintext Primary Account Numbers (PAN) and Card Verification Values in application logs.
suggestedFix: Introduce a structured audit logger with automatic tokenization and masking, sanitizing card numbers to `****-****-****-1234` and dropping CVV entirely from log payloads.

title: Unhandled Async Rejections & Missing Fault Boundaries
description: Third-party notification and webhook calls are invoked without proper `.catch()` handling or circuit breaker logic, causing unhandled promise rejections that can terminate the Node.js process.
justification: A transient third-party webhook failure must never bring down the core checkout API or fail an already captured customer transaction.
suggestedFix: Wrap peripheral notifications in an isolated resilience boundary that catches errors, queues retries with exponential backoff, and returns a structured `Result<T, E>` monad.
refactoredReference: Lines 240-270 in RefactoredOrderPipeline.ts (Result monad & resilient event dispatch)

title: Unbounded Memory Leak in Global Audit Cache
fowlerPattern: Replace Unbounded Collection with LRU Bounded Buffer
description: A global array `auditHistory = []` continuously appends every completed order payload without eviction or size boundary. Over prolonged server execution, this triggers Garbage Collection thrashing and inevitable Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes.
justification: Memory footprint grows linearly with processed throughput ($O(N)$ memory leak), degrading server stability in high-throughput environments.
suggestedFix: Replace the raw unbounded array with a bounded ring buffer or time-windowed Least Recently Used (LRU) storage strategy with configurable maximum capacity.
